results.transcript: I've gotten a ton of questions about the MediCube Booster Pro X2, so let me answer the top ones. And this is proudly sponsored by MediCube, so thank you for that. What's new versus the original? Three modes, dual, mask, and AI, plus a treatment head that's 30% larger, so you finish your treatments faster. Is it worth upgrading? For me, it's the dual mode. You can run two technologies at once, so you can boost absorption while firming in the same session. It basically cuts your treatment time in half. How does the booster mode work? It's electroporation. It creates tiny temporary pathways so your serums actually penetrate instead of setting on top. I pair it with lightweight peptide, PDRN, or NAD serums. And how about mask mode? It pushes sheet mask ingredients deeper, so five minutes does what usually would take 20. Where do I start? The new AI mode. It picks the mode and the intensity for your goals. MediCube Booster Pro X2 is not magic, and it's not for everyone, but if you're already consistent and have five minutes a day, it helps you get more from the skincare that you already use.

results.caption: #SKITTLES_Partner Toronto Pride was one for the books🌈🥹 Between playing my first Toronto Pride DJ set, running around Church Street, and celebrating with the queer community all weekend, it was one of those weekends I know I’ll remember for a long time #ad One of my favourite stops was the @skittles Celebrate the Rainbow experience at the Pride Street Fair. From free samples and live performances to the interactive rainbow wall, it was such a fun way tocelebrate Pride and self-expression. I also loved adding my own message to the “Celebrate the Rainbow, Taste the Rainbow” wall. For every sticker added throughout the weekend, Skittles donated $2 to Rainbow Railroad (up to $15,000) to help support LGBTQI+ individuals facing persecution around the world. And if you’re craving a bag after watching this, you can grab your favourite Skittles @Walmart Canada. #CelebrateTheRainbow #TorontoPride
results.transcript: Let's go to Toronto Pride. Except this year, I'm fully graduating from the professional shower pop star to full on stage pop star. But first things first, I wanna hang out with my people. And every time I get into the city, the first thing that I do, even if it's just for an hour, is I head to Church Street. They have so many installations, performances, booths that give back to the community. Little special mention to the Skittles booths that gave $2 for every sticker placed on the Rainbow Arch to Rainbow Railroad. I'm so thankful for Pride because look at all the talented, amazing gay people in my life. All right now. Ladies, gentlemen, and everyone in between, let's welcome to the stage, Genevieve La Force. You guys, I am a theater gay turned DJ gay. What can I say? I just played an entire set in front of a bunch of lesbians and I soft launched my own song. Oop, spoiler alert. I'm so grateful for this community, for Pride and to brands like Skittles that continue to support the LGBTQ plus community. So if you're celebrating this year, grab a bag of Skittles at your local Walmart and celebrate the rainbow.
